anomalies.observed: C8 is valued "1mF/25V" (1 millifarad) in a 0805 capacitor footprint, on the EPD-side net Net-(C8-Pad1) that goes to J1.5. The SPICE deck also models it as 1mF.
anomalies.expected: The spec lists C8 with the other 1 µF/25 V EPD capacitors (C1/C5/C7/C8/C9/C10 = 1 µF/25 V). A 1 mF ceramic cannot fit in an 0805 package at 25 V, so the value is a clear error.
anomalies.impact: If the wrong value were fitted, the bypass/filter on the display-driver rail would be mis-sized, and a 0805 part cannot carry the stated 1 mF value, so the rail would be decoupled incorrectly.

anomalies.observed: The SPICE stimulus sets the battery node to 25.0 V DC (V_BAT_ BAT+ 0 DC 25.0).
anomalies.expected: The spec describes a single 18650 Li-ion cell powering BAT+, which is about 3.7 V nominal (roughly 4.2 V full). The FAN53610 VIN is rated for about 5.5 V, so 25 V is far outside the intended input.

evidence.quote: Single-cell Li-ion battery holder ... 18650 Li-ion cell

anomalies.impact: Any simulation driven from this source would apply an over-voltage to the regulator input, giving misleading results and suggesting the design was not verified at the intended battery voltage.

anomalies.observed: C11 is a 0.1 µF capacitor, but its footprint is an inductor pad pattern (Inductor_SMD:L_0805...). Its pin 1 is on a no-connect net, so only one side is connected to GND.
anomalies.expected: A decoupling capacitor should use a capacitor footprint, and both of its pins should be connected to meaningful nets.
anomalies.impact: The part is electrically ineffective because one terminal floats, and the wrong footprint could cause assembly errors.

parsed.summary: The netlist has a clearly wrong value on C8 (1 mF in an 0805 where the spec calls for 1 µF/25 V), and the SPICE deck drives the battery node at 25 V where the spec describes a single 18650 cell. A capacitor C11 also has an inductor footprint and a floating terminal.
